name: Replace the Numbers
description: You have an array of integers (initially empty). You have to perform $$$q$$$ queries. Each query is of one of two types: "$$$1$$$ $$$x$$$" — add the element $$$x$$$ to the end of the array; "$$$2$$$ $$$x$$$ $$$y$$$" — replace all occurrences of $$$x$$$ in the array with $$$y$$$. Find the resulting array after performing all the queries.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$q$$$ ($$$1 \le q \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of queries. Next $$$q$$$ lines contain queries (one per line). Each query is of one of two types: "$$$1$$$ $$$x$$$" ($$$1 \le x \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$); "$$$2$$$ $$$x$$$ $$$y$$$" ($$$1 \le x, y \le 5 \cdot 10^5$$$). It's guaranteed that there is at least one query of the first type.
output_specification: In a single line, print $$$k$$$ integers — the resulting array after performing all the queries, where $$$k$$$ is the number of queries of the first type.
approach_summary: Maintain disjoint sets using path compression and union by rank/size. Process edge additions and component queries in O(α(N)) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1620E — Replace the Numbers [80. DSU / Union Find]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Connectivity is an equivalence relation. By organizing connected components into trees and merging smaller trees into larger ones (`union-by-rank/size`) combined with path compression, find and union operations run in near-constant inverse Ackermann time $O(\alpha(N))$.
